newsitem.title: PERU: Peru coffee body sees '97 exports value up 35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Peru coffee body sees '97 exports value up 35 pct.

text.p: The private Peruvian Coffee Chamber predicted Monday that the value of Peru's coffee exports would rise by 35 percent this year to a total $300 million.
The chamber said in a statement this would be due to bigger national production -- thanks to better climatic conditions in growing areas and cyclical conditions -- and a higher export price.
Peru exported 2.18 million quintals of coffee, worth $223 million, in 1996, and 2.31 million quintals, worth $286 million, the previous year. One quintal is equivalent to 46 kg.
The chamber said that 1997 production was expected to rise by 15 percent compared to the previous year, but did not specify 1996's total output.
It predicted that the average export price for Peruvian coffee would be $140 per quintal in 1997, up from $102.32 last year and $123.88 in 1995.
